classification: one-prompt actual-activation reduction screen informed by inspected SM89 SASS; partial numerical match only, not an exact kernel reconstruction

sass_observations.observed_sequence: The disassembly contains packed HMUL2 operations, HADD2.F32 conversions of half lanes, FADD.FTZ accumulation, SHFL.DOWN warp reductions, then FP16 output conversion/store. One FFMA.FTZ is present in each template and appears in scaling/dequant setup; the product/accumulation path contains HMUL2 and FADD, not an FFMA dot-product chain.
sass_observations.interpretation: This supports testing FP16-rounded products followed by FP32 accumulation. M=1 and M=3 are distinct compiled templates with different instruction counts and layout, even though prior actual-input checks found row outputs invariant between them.

lane_strided_fp16_product_screen.interpretation: All tested lane counts match the corresponding half-product/full-K candidate count (677/768); changing lane count does not expose the remaining BNB accumulation behavior in this probe.

interpretation: Rounding each reconstructed FP16 product before FP32 summation increases matches to 677/768 (88.2%) at 256 channels and 2679/3072 (87.2%) at 1024 channels.

The best simple schedule remains non-exact; SASS supports half-product rounding as one relevant numerical boundary but does not reveal enough runtime state to reconstruct the precise quantized dequantization and reduction order.
The reduction tile sizes tested after FP16 product rounding yield identical match counts in this probe; this does not establish that their per-value reduction order is equivalent.
limits: One prompt, first-layer gate projection, and three forced token rows; output channels 0–255 or 0–1023.
